note: Executable return-link configuration examples. Every example is validated by bin/check_config.py against ob.contract; out-of-range values must be rejected, never defaulted.

examples.name: healthy_baseline
examples.intent: Wired baseline: no impairment. Documents the 200 ms budget -> 200000 us and 600000 B bounded queue (~2.9 s of media).

examples.name: weak_jitter_120ms
examples.intent: 120 ms jitter + 20 ms base delay: budget must exceed the one-way jitter envelope so out-of-order arrivals still play.

examples.name: weak_burst_loss_under_budget
examples.intent: Gilbert-Elliott bursts: budget covers retransmission of a burst; late-drop counter should stay low.

examples.name: weak_severe_over_budget
examples.intent: Deliberately under-budget: 25% bad state + 150 ms jitter. Demonstrates that loss at least as long as the budget is NOT recoverable and will show up as frame gaps / late drops.

examples.name: short_outage_inside_budget
examples.intent: 1.2 s blackhole with a 2 s budget: SRT can retransmit the withheld packets; the loss interval should stay near one retransmission window, not the full outage.

examples.name: short_outage_over_budget
examples.intent: Same 1.2 s blackhole with a 250 ms budget: most of the outage is unrecoverable; expect a visible media gap of roughly the outage length.

examples.name: long_outage_rebuild
examples.intent: 15 s blackhole: session teardown + rebuild is expected; recovery resumes at the live edge with a visible gap. No continuity promise is made.
